html:
Maryse Conde was a novelist born in Pointe-a-Pitre, Guadeloupe, in 1934. Her books on Africa and the Caribbean made her one of the best known writers in French.

She lived for years in West Africa, in Guinea, Ghana and Senegal. Her novel Segu (1984), about a Bambara family in the Mali of the 1700s and 1800s, became a best seller. I, Tituba, Black Witch of Salem told of an enslaved woman from Barbados caught in the Salem witch trials.

She taught at Columbia University in New York and won the New Academy Prize in Literature in 2018, given in a year when the Nobel was not. She wrote of the links between Africa, the Atlantic slave trade and the islands, and of the creole world described by Glissant.
